name: Boiled Custard
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: Yolks of five eggs and the whites of seven
ingredients.originalText: Yolks of five eggs and the whites of seven

ingredients.name: Vanilla flavoring—1 teaspoonful to the pint
ingredients.originalText: Vanilla flavoring—1 teaspoonful to the pint

instructions.text: Heat the milk almost to boiling
Beat the yolks light and stir in the sugar
Add the milk in the manner described in general directions at head of this section
Stir in five whites whipped stiff
Return to the fire and stir until thick, but not until it breaks
Whip the whites of two eggs to a méringue with a heaping tablespoonful of powdered sugar
When the custard is cold, pile a little of this upon the top of each cup
You may lay a preserved strawberry or cherry, or a bit of melon sweetmeat, or a little bright jelly upon each

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Heat the milk almost to boiling
2. Beat the yolks light and stir in the sugar
3. Add the milk in the manner described in general directions at head of this section
4. Stir in five whites whipped stiff
5. Return to the fire and stir until thick, but not until it breaks
6. Season it with vanilla
7. Pour into glass cups
8. Whip the whites of two eggs to a méringue with a heaping tablespoonful of powdered sugar
9. When the custard is cold, pile a little of this upon the top of each cup
10. You may lay a preserved strawberry or cherry, or a bit of melon sweetmeat, or a little bright jelly upon each
